cards.title: Building a list in a loop
cards.body: Use a `for` loop with `range` to work out a value each round and append it.
cards.code:
tens = []
for i in range(1, 4):
    tens.append(i * 10)
print(tens)

cards.title: One append, one item
cards.body: Each `append` adds exactly one item, so after the loop the list has one item per round.

check.question: What does this print?
check.code:
s = []
for i in range(1, 4):
    s.append(i + i)
print(s)
check.explanation: Each round appends i + i: 2, then 4, then 6.

exercise.prompt: Read N, build a list of the squares 1, 4, 9, … up to N × N using `append`, then print it with the numbers separated by spaces.
exercise.starterCode:
n = int(input())
squares = []
# append the squares of 1 to n
print(" ".join(map(str, squares)))
